evals.prompt: Review a 65,536-token Evo2 RL qualification. The driver preprocesses successfully after a local modification, but a newly spawned Ray worker allocates [1,1,L,L] boolean attention storage. After generation with kv_cache_management_mode=offload, the next training forward enters a decode CUDA graph; an adapter also reports that its model storage must remain resident. A teammate proposes halving context and ignoring EOS. Give the smallest repair and qualification proposal; do not launch anything.
evals.expected_output: A worker-local preprocessing and graph/cache lifecycle repair that preserves the scientific workload.
assertions: Identifies the approximately 4 GiB quadratic boolean mask and installs implicit-causal inputs in fresh workers as well as the driver, preserving absolute positions and action/loss masks.
Detaches decode-only graph managers before training and restores them for subsequent generation; distinguishes manager reuse from invalidating runners tied to released cache storage.
Honors nonpersistent model offload despite an adapter residency request and uses matching patched runtime/adapter code, rather than relying on a configuration label.

Rejects context reduction or EOS removal as equivalent repairs; requires causal output/gradient parity, fresh-worker checks and repeated full-shape rollout/replay/update plus save/reload evidence before claiming qualification.

evals.prompt: Review this local execution proposal for full-genome SFT followed by RL; provide corrected paths and sizing without launching. Eight 80-GiB GPUs are visible, but an existing job owns GPUs 0–3 until 18:00. /repo is read-only; /scratch is writable with 1.5 TB free and is erased at job exit; /results is durable/writable with 620 GB free; /cache is durable/writable with 110 GB free. Estimated footprint: downloaded assets 180 GB, retained checkpoints 240 GB, logs/final outputs 20 GB, disposable scorer work 300 GB. The draft stores everything in /scratch and requests all eight GPUs now. Full-shape measurements exist only for eight GPUs. The approved context and global batch must remain fixed.
evals.expected_output: A feasible storage and execution decision that accounts for occupancy, durability, and missing four-GPU measurements.
assertions: Places the 180 GB assets, 240 GB retained checkpoints, and 20 GB durable outputs within available durable capacity, for example /results; does not fit 180 GB assets into 110 GB /cache.
Limits /scratch to the 300 GB discardable work and identifies a writable checkout/build location because /repo is read-only.
Does not claim eight GPUs are available now or assume the eight-GPU capacity evidence validates a four-GPU run.
Proposes waiting for the allocation or a bounded full-shape four-GPU qualification that preserves context/global batch through supported topology and accumulation, with durable job/log paths.

evals.prompt: Review these two inventory records. The agent container reports nvidia-smi: command not found, no /dev/nvidia entries, torch.cuda.is_available=false. A scheduler inventory from ten minutes ago lists node cedar with 8 H100s, state IDLE, and an authorized host-side read-only probe is available; no host probe has yet run. The operator asks whether to install a driver or schedule a CPU fallback. Give the next diagnostic command and the conclusions justified now.
evals.expected_output: A host-visible diagnostic proposal that separates container visibility from actual hardware status.
assertions: Treats the container failures as a visibility limit, not proof of missing GPUs or broken host drivers; also does not treat scheduler inventory alone as a live functional probe.
Proposes a host-context nvidia-smi/device/CUDA check using the already-authorized facility without seeking redundant approval.
Defers driver installation and CPU/topology changes until the host evidence resolves the conflict.
If the proposed probe cannot be performed, explicitly leaves current hardware readiness unknown and provides an operator-executable check.

evals.prompt: A reconnect finds Slurm job 48172 owned by this project, state RUNNING, stdout /results/R/logs/48172.out. The log advanced from optimizer 80 to 88 in 40 minutes; validation/save occurs every 20 steps. /results/R/decision.json says step 80, decision=stop, reason='comparable validation divergence'. The submission wrapper has an unconditional requeue loop. The chat's old SSH shell is gone, and W&B has not updated for an hour. Give a recovery and handoff proposal using this snapshot, without submitting or cancelling anything.
evals.expected_output: A durable-job handoff that detects continued work past a recorded stop and avoids duplicate launches.
assertions: Recognizes job 48172 as still running from scheduler and trainer evidence despite stale W&B; does not launch a replacement on reconnect.

Flags updates 81–88 after the step 80 stop as a supervisor-control failure and proposes stopping the existing trainer through the scheduler's scoped cancellation path plus disabling unconditional continuation.
Provides concrete status/log/cancel references tied to 48172 and /results/R, preserving the best and latest useful checkpoints and original stop evidence.
Uses the observed five minutes per update and next decision horizon to justify a useful monitoring cadence, rather than rapid liveness polling or declaring submission/completion synonymous.

evals.prompt: Choose a screening resource proposal from this synthetic benchmark. The job has 32 scheduler CPUs although the host exposes 192. OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 is inherited. For one whole-genome safety tool, 8 workers × 8 threads gives 14 records/min and 28 GiB RSS; 4×6 gives 21/min and 20 GiB; 2×12 gives 18/min and 18 GiB. A separate ORF caller has no benchmark. One design goal's 384 eligible genomes span two prompt lengths; whole-pool MMseqs takes 70 s at 24 threads. Shared-filesystem temp cleanup takes 160 s/batch versus 9 s on node-local scratch. Durable output size is small. A teammate proposes splitting MMseqs by GPU and using 192 workers. Review it.
evals.expected_output: A measured CPU, pool, and scratch allocation proposal that preserves scoring semantics.
assertions: Uses 32 scheduler CPUs, not 192 host CPUs or inherited OMP=2, as the allocation ceiling; favors the measured 4×6 option with headroom over 8×8 oversubscription.
Budgets MMseqs 24 threads against concurrent work, either scheduling it separately or bounding other work to the remaining CPUs.
Keeps all 384 eligible genomes for this goal in one diversity pool; rejects GPU/prompt sharding because it changes cluster sizes and rewards.

Uses local scratch for disposable cleanup-heavy work while keeping logs, failures, and final results durable; identifies the ORF caller as requiring its own bounded benchmark rather than inheriting safety-tool tuning.

evals.prompt: Review a container setup draft. Host GPUs pass nvidia-smi and Docker's NVIDIA runtime test; host Python lacks the recipe dependencies and may not be changed. Checkout is /work/recipes, data /datasets (read-only), results /runs (writable), cache /cache (writable). The draft builds dependencies from the image's baked /opt/recipes, then mounts /work/recipes at /workspace and runs that newer checkout with host Python through docker exec. The recipe Dockerfile is available. Give a corrected build/activation/mount sketch; no image build is requested.
evals.expected_output: A container proposal whose installed code matches the mounted checkout and leaves host Python untouched.
assertions: Uses a GPU-enabled recipe Dockerfile or supported NVIDIA PyTorch environment with explicit mounts for the given checkout/data/results/cache paths.
Builds with ./.ci_build.sh inside the mounted checkout and activates that checkout's .ci_test_env.sh before recipe commands.
Identifies baked /opt/recipes versus mounted /workspace as a code/dependency alignment risk and removes the host-Python execution path.
Records image identity and mount/activation details sufficient for the same runtime to be reconstructed, without claiming a successful build from this draft.

evals.prompt: An aarch64 GPU container starts correctly. The asset manifest points MMseqs to /cache/x86_64/mmseqs/bin/mmseqs; file reports ELF64 x86-64 and executing it gives Exec format error. A separate dependency install under --no-build-isolation fails resolving Biotite/Biotraj distributions, then says ModuleNotFoundError: hatchling during a source attempt. Other packages have compatible wheels. Propose the smallest supported environment repair and its validation.
evals.expected_output: An architecture-correct asset setup and conditional source-build fallback.
assertions: Rejects reuse of the x86_64 cache and uses the maintained aarch64-selected downloads/architecture-qualified paths for affected native assets.
Uses the documented biotite 0.41.2/biotraj 1.2.2 fallback for the observed packaging failure, not an unconditional pin for every platform.

Explicitly enables the commented Hatchling, hatch-vcs, and hatch-cython prerequisites for this observed source-build fallback under --no-build-isolation; leaves them disabled for normal wheel installs instead of treating the Python error as a GPU-driver problem.
Requires native executable architecture/version checks and import tests in the actual runtime; preserves working wheel paths where no fallback is needed.

evals.prompt: Review a coherent-memory ARM node failure. numactl reports node 0: CPUs 0–71, DRAM; node 1: no CPUs, HBM. CUDA allocated/reserved stays 54/58 GiB across save 1, but node 1 Cached grows from 4 to 39 GiB and the next allocation fails. A pre-save two-update test passed. The non-root job also gets Permission denied compiling a dataset helper under /opt/env. Docker build context is 900 GB because it includes results/. The runtime must stay non-root. Give a diagnosis and qualification proposal.
evals.expected_output: A memory-placement and build proposal tested across checkpoint lifecycle boundaries.
assertions: Connects the post-save HBM Cached growth with CPU/page-cache placement on the memory-only node as a supported hypothesis, while noting CUDA allocation alone cannot explain total residency.
Proposes supported CPU/offload/cache placement on node 0 while retaining device-required memory-node visibility, with actual residency measurements to confirm the cause.
Requires a lifecycle crossing save 1, following update, save 2, and fresh-process restart before claiming capacity; pre-save fit is insufficient.
Builds architecture-specific dataset helpers while the image is writable and import-tests as the runtime UID; excludes generated 900 GB results from the build context and mounts them at runtime.

evals.prompt: Assess a policy-training microbatch failure for an RL deployment that alternates full-genome rollouts and optimizer updates, runs periodic validation, and saves resumable checkpoints. Before launch: GPU 0 used 31 GiB/free 49 GiB, compute PID list empty; identical GPU 1 used 0.6 GiB/free 79.4 GiB. During the first optimizer update of a full-shape run on GPU 0, the job reports allocated 42 GiB/reserved 45 GiB and an OOM on a 6 GiB request. After exit GPU 0 returns to 31 GiB. No authority to kill external processes is granted. The proposed record says 'microbatch 2 exceeds 80 GiB; retry microbatch 1.' What should the capacity record and next test say?
evals.expected_output: A confounded capacity diagnosis and a clean-device comparison without unauthorized cleanup.
assertions: Accounts for the 31 GiB baseline external/platform occupancy separately from the job's 42/45 GiB allocator footprint; does not conclude microbatch 2 intrinsically needs more than 80 GiB.
Proposes the same full-shape microbatch 2 test on the available clean GPU or an appropriately authorized clean allocation, rather than unapproved process killing.

Does not infer ownership or reclaimability from the empty compute-PID list and leaves external allocations untouched. A clean-device comparison may proceed without resolving the external owner's identity; host/device inspection is needed if the proposal depends on reclaiming that memory.
Requires the eventual test to include optimizer, validation, save/reload transitions and records baseline plus job allocation before choosing a smaller microbatch.

evals.prompt: Review this runtime matrix; these are measured local results, not a general compatibility claim. Host driver R550 cannot be changed. ImageA/CUDA 13.3 fails CUDA initialization; ImageB/CUDA 13.1 passes. ImageB bundles cuDNN 9.19, required kernel probe needs at least 9.24, and recipe .venv contains 9.27. After setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH, rank 0 reports 9.27 but ranks 1–7 report 9.19 and fail the kernel probe. Propose a reproducible distributed startup fix and the evidence needed to accept it.
evals.expected_output: A locally driver-compatible image and consistent process-start library selection across all workers.
assertions: Selects measured-working ImageB and preserves the required kernel instead of changing the fixed host driver or retrying ImageA.

Diagnoses inconsistent worker activation/library loading from the rank split and proposes recipe environment propagation plus an explicit startup selection such as LD_PRELOAD for its libcudnn.so.9 where needed.
Requires effective Torch CUDA/cuDNN versions and the required kernel probe on all eight workers; rank 0 success alone does not qualify the runtime.
Includes the chosen image and library/activation contract in proposed resume configuration without asserting all R550 hosts universally support the listed CUDA version.
